title: Rocks From the Moon's Far Side Help Solve a Mystery
summary:
The side of the Moon we see from Earth looks very different from the side that always faces away. The near side has big, dark plains of old volcanic rock. The far side is rough, with lots of craters and a thicker crust.

In 2024, China's Chang'e-6 mission brought back the first rocks from the far side. A team led by Professor Hejiu Hui of Nanjing University studied them and compared them with near side rocks.

Deep inside, both sides seem very similar. But the outer layer, the crust, is different.

The scientists think they know why. Long ago, the Moon was covered by an ocean of melted rock. Later, the same side began to always face Earth. Earth was much closer then, and its gravity heated the near side more. This uneven heat stirred huge flows of melted rock and helped give the Moon two different faces.
why_it_matters: Next time you look at the Moon, you will know its far side looks very different, and why.

keywords.explanation: Volcanic describes rock or land made by volcanoes and lava.
Craters are bowl-shaped holes made when space rocks crash into a surface.
The crust is the hard outer layer of a planet or moon.
A mission is a planned trip to do a special job, like collecting rocks in space.
Gravity is the force that pulls things toward each other, like a ball falling to the ground.
